Definition: hamlets of Jair, a region of Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Havoth-jair, the villages of Jair, are the towns Jair the son of Manasseh took and named after himself. They are counted in the settlement east of Jordan, in the record of the conquest, and again in the days of Jair the judge, whose thirty sons rode on thirty colts and held thirty cities.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the villages of Jair outlasted Jair himself, and the name stayed on the land. What God gives His people to name, He lets them keep.
RelatedEvents: Reuben and Gad Settle East of the Jordan; The Defeat of Sihon and Og; Jair, Judge of Israel
